text:
Marathon Petroleum gained 2.8% today, bouncing back after a sharp 6.97% drop over the last two weeks. The recovery came as U.S. oil held around $103 per barrel and refineries ran at 92.8% capacity—high enough to support solid margins—while news emerged of potential de-escalation talks between the U.S. and Iran. The latter matters because reduced Middle East tensions could ease concerns about disrupted oil supplies that have pushed crude prices higher, which had weighed on the refiner's stock earlier in the week.

The broader context is tension between fuel supply tightness (which normally boosts refiner profits) and investor caution about Big Oil earnings. A leadership change at Marathon was announced this week, and while surging refining margins have helped the industry weather higher crude costs, markets are pricing in uncertainty around whether those profits can hold or if guidance disappoints when companies report.
